maps.name: Normandy: Link the Beachheads
maps.description: 6–12 June 1944 — Link the beachheads: capture Carentan and Bayeux.
maps.objective: Link the beachheads: capture Carentan and Bayeux.

maps.history: From September 1942 the German Sixth Army fought its way into Stalingrad and pushed the 62nd Army back to a strip of the Volga bank, but never took the whole city. maps.name: Gaugamela: Alexander Charges
maps.description: 1 October 331 BCE — Capture Darius's camp.
maps.objective: Capture Darius's camp.
maps.history: At Gaugamela in 331 BCE Alexander the Great beat a much larger Persian army under Darius III. When the Persian left followed his move to the right, a gap opened and Alexander charged through it toward Darius, who fled.

maps.name: Thermopylae: The Hot Gates
maps.description: 480 BCE — Hold the Hot Gates for 5:00.
maps.objective: Hold the Hot Gates for 5:00.
maps.history: In 480 BCE a Greek army led by Leonidas of Sparta held the pass of Thermopylae against Xerxes for three days, until a local guide led the Persians over the mountain path behind them.

maps.name: Salamis: The Narrow Strait
maps.description: September 480 BCE — Sink the Persian fleet.
maps.objective: Sink the Persian fleet.
maps.history: In September 480 BCE Themistocles lured the Persian fleet into the strait of Salamis, where the Greek triremes, fewer but better handled in the narrow water, broke it while Xerxes watched from the shore. The defeat ended the Persian invasion by sea.

maps.name: Cannae: The Double Envelopment
maps.description: 2 August 216 BCE — Hold Cannae for 5:00.
maps.objective: Hold Cannae for 5:00.
maps.history: On 2 August 216 BCE Hannibal let a much larger Roman army push into the centre of his line at Cannae, then closed his African infantry on its flanks and his cavalry on its rear. Most of the Roman army was killed or captured.

maps.name: Hastings: Senlac Ridge

maps.objective: Break the shield wall: capture Senlac ridge and Caldbec Hill.
maps.history: On 14 October 1066 William of Normandy defeated King Harold's English army on Senlac ridge near Hastings. Parts of the English line broke ranks to pursue retreating Normans and were cut down; Harold was killed late in the day.

maps.name: Agincourt: The Muddy Field
maps.description: 25 October 1415 — Hold Maisoncelle for 5:00.
maps.objective: Hold Maisoncelle for 5:00.
maps.history: On 25 October 1415 Henry V's outnumbered English army defeated the French at Agincourt. The French attacked across a muddy, narrowing field and were shot down by English archers before they reached the line.
maps.adaptation: Scaled RTS adaptation: geography, force sizes and time are compressed. Each era fights with its own troops; scripted waves stand for the formations of the day rather than exact orders of battle.

maps.name: Stirling Bridge: Catch Them Crossing
maps.description: 11 September 1297 — Capture Stirling and the English camp.
maps.objective: Capture Stirling and the English camp.
maps.history: On 11 September 1297 the English army of the Earl of Surrey began crossing the narrow bridge over the Forth at Stirling. When about half of it was over, Wallace and Moray charged, seized the bridge end and destroyed the vanguard; the rest of the English army fell back.

maps.name: Hattin: The Springs
maps.description: 4 July 1187 — Hold Kafr Hattin and Tiberias for 5:00.
maps.objective: Hold Kafr Hattin and Tiberias for 5:00.
maps.history: On 4 July 1187 Saladin trapped the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, exhausted by thirst, on the plateau below the Horns of Hattin. Count Raymond of Tripoli broke out with a few knights; the rest of the army was destroyed or captured, and Jerusalem fell that autumn.

maps.description: 2 December 1805 — Seize the Pratzen Heights, then take Austerlitz.
maps.objective: Seize the Pratzen Heights, then take Austerlitz.
maps.history: On 2 December 1805 Napoleon drew the Russian and Austrian armies into attacking his weakened right, then broke their centre on the Pratzen Heights. Austerlitz ended the War of the Third Coalition.

maps.description: 18 June 1815 — Hold Mont-Saint-Jean for 5:00 until the Prussians arrive.
maps.objective: Hold Mont-Saint-Jean for 5:00 until the Prussians arrive.
maps.history: On 18 June 1815 Wellington's Anglo-allied army held the ridge at Mont-Saint-Jean against repeated French attacks until Blücher's Prussians arrived on Napoleon's flank. The defeat of the Imperial Guard ended Napoleon's rule.

maps.objective: Capture the Bagration flèches and the Great Redoubt.
maps.history: At Borodino on 7 September 1812 Napoleon's army stormed the Russian earthworks after a day of repeated assaults: Bagration's flèches fell in the morning and the Great Redoubt in the afternoon, at terrible cost on both sides. maps.objective: Sink the Combined Fleet.
maps.history: On 21 October 1805 Nelson's fleet attacked the Franco-Spanish Combined Fleet off Cape Trafalgar in two columns, broke its line and captured or destroyed eighteen ships without losing one. Nelson was killed in the battle.
